clue.text: Agreed to be taught at university around the north

indicators.note: around says the first pair of pieces is wrapped about the next one

parts.note: to take a subject is to be taught it
up means in residence at university
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to study at a northern university.
explanation.walkthrough: You take a subject when you are taught it, and 'up' is the old phrase for being in residence at university. 'around' means the two words go round the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To have taken up an offer is to have accepted it, so the phrase is a synonym for agreed.

clue.text: What a nark may do is endless?

definitions.meaning: a nark is a police informer, who gives a warning to the police
with its tip removed, a thing has lost its end

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an informer's work never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informers give the police secret warnings, and a thing with its point cut away has had its tip removed.

clue.text: Venomous type? Man has company support

parts.note: a king is a man in chess
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A dangerous sort of fellow is backed by his firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, an example of a poisonous species.

clue.text: One working for Portia when father JAMA and knight turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: as means when, as in as he arrived
a sire is a father
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A servant appears when Portia's father and a knight arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ASSIREN; the stray JAMA is an OCR artefact, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is Portia's waiting-woman in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, a lady's maid in her service.

clue.text: Remarkable things -— number collected by macho types in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in says the rest sits inside the state abbreviation
collected by says the first piece is gathered inside the second

parts.note: he-men are macho men

explanation.surface: Wonders as a number are rounded up by tough guys in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected by' means the macho types go round the number; 'in' then puts all of that inside the state's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable or extraordinary occurrences, a recognised sense of the plural.

clue.text: Have the assembled groups succeeded?

parts.note: posses are groups of men assembled to help a sheriff
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A question of whether the gathered teams have won.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Chaplain in flat on outskirts of Reigate

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A clergyman lives in an apartment on the edge of Reigate.
explanation.walkthrough: Reigate is a town in Surrey; its first and last letters are R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal name for a military chaplain.

clue.text: Everyone in revue is superficial

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a revue is a type of show
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A criticism that a revue's whole cast is shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow means lacking depth, a synonym of superficial.

clue.text: Trimmed privet, top being cut by daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: privet is a shrub grown as a hedge

explanation.surface: A daughter clips the top of a privet hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: Edged means given a trimmed border, as a lawn neatened at its edges.

clue.text: Commercial interrupting tranquil piece JUMPI of music

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'Commercial interrupting tranquil piece JUMPI of music': the stray JUMPI splits the definition 'piece of music'; the scan is unreadable and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Commercial interrupting tranquil piece JUMPI of music

clue.text: Foreign correspondent, unsettled, heading off to China?

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an unsettled question is an open one
china (china plate) is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so a friend

explanation.surface: A disturbed overseas reporter departs for China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims O from OPEN to give PEN. China here is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is someone abroad you exchange letters with, a correspondent in the letter-writing sense.

clue.text: Fury shown as lid is missing from crate

indicators.note: a lid is the top, so the top letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: crate is slang for a decrepit car, as is banger, British slang for an old car

explanation.surface: Someone is furious because the top has gone from a packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: A crate is not a box but an old banger (British slang for a battered car); 'lid is missing from' drops its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is extreme anger, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Mugs, fine ones

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A remark that some mugs are nice ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for face, so mugs are faces.

clue.text: Once again, left Yemeni port with too much on board

parts.note: over means again, as in do it over
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship again leaves Aden heavily overloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means carrying too heavy a load, as a vessel with too much cargo.

clue.text: Novel and daring symphony?

parts.note: brave and daring are synonyms
Dvorak's Symphony No 9 is From the New World

explanation.surface: Something both original and bold might be a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: Aldous Huxley's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's dystopian book of that title is a famous example of a novel.

clue.text: Odd, Eric pinching c-coin of little value che

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'Odd, Eric pinching c-coin of little value che': 'c-coin' and the trailing 'che' are OCR garble; the scan is unreadable and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Odd, Eric pinching c-coin of little value che

clue.text: Hand out small beer in grounds?

parts.note: to ration is to hand out in fixed portions
ale is beer; small beer is weak ale

explanation.surface: Distributing weak beer at a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' looks like a playing field but means reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind something, its grounds or basis.

clue.text: Arachnid in house, note

parts.note: Scorpio is one of the zodiac signs, called houses in astrology

explanation.surface: A spider-like creature lives in a house, a note warns.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion belongs to the class of arachnids, like spiders and mites.

clue.text: Credit arrangement of Tennyson's Light Brigade?

definitions.meaning: a shop arrangement letting a customer buy now and pay later
Tennyson's poem is an account of a cavalry charge, The Charge of the Light Brigade

explanation.surface: A financial deal somehow linked to the doomed cavalry of Tennyson's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A store account on which purchases are charged is a credit facility; read literally it is a narrative of a charge.

clue.text: Swine holding queue up is an unusually tall person

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole is read from the bottom upwards
holding says the first piece contains the second

parts.note: a hog is a swine
a queue is a pigtail, a tail of hair

explanation.surface: A pig is keeping a line of people waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: A queue in the old sense is a pigtail. 'holding' gives HTAILOG and 'up' turns it round, reading from the bottom of a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath, the Philistine giant slain by David, is used for any very large person.

clue.text: Doubtful, pawnbroker, over a radiogram at first

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece stands above the rest

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker is unsure about an old radiogram.
explanation.walkthrough: A radiogram is an old radio and record player cabinet; 'Uncle' was slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear means not certain, a synonym for doubtful.

clue.text: Put down good character

definitions.meaning: to put something down to a person is to attribute it to them
a good reputation, as in to your honour

explanation.surface: Disparaging someone of fine reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit is to ascribe or put down to someone, and credit is also standing or good name.

clue.text: About to call one about coup

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to bell is to ring someone, to call them
I is the Roman numeral one
on means about, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: Someone is about to phone a friend about an overthrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is an uprising against those in power, and a rebellion is much the same kind of revolt.

clue.text: Pipe in coffin stand holding king

indicators.note: holding says the first piece contains the second

parts.note: a bier is a stand for a coffin
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A pipe in a funeral stand holds a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier is a tobacco pipe made from the root of the briar heath, so an example of a pipe.

clue.text: Victor letting drop wife's secret

indicators.note: letting drop says the letter is removed

parts.note: the victor is the winner

explanation.surface: A champion lets slip his wife's secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner means private or concealed, as one's inner feelings are secret.

clue.text: Group of singers sing endlessly about love

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes round the next piece
endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to chirp is to sing like a bird
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A group sings without stopping about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CHIRP to CHIR, and 'about' wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, exactly a group of them.

clue.text: Article on business on one Balearic island

indicators.note: on again places business after the following piece
on in an across clue means placed after the piece that follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
biz is slang for business, as in showbiz
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on trade on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so the order runs I, BIZ, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, an example of the type.

clue.text: She may attend to babe in arms due for a change

indicators.note: the letters of these words are to be changed round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carer comes to a baby that needs changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' suggests a nappy, but it signals an anagram of IN ARMS DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, so she tends to babies.

clue.text: Storm's in Cwmbran or the Rhondda

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gale is raging in two Welsh places.
explanation.walkthrough: Cwmbran and the Rhondda are places in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A norther is a strong cold wind or storm blowing from the north.

clue.text: Right a wrong, right?

definitions.meaning: to put right a mistake is to amend it
right as an adjective, meaning accurate

explanation.surface: A query whether redressing an injustice is proper.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct an error is to put it right, and correct also means accurate.
